newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean 3-yr yields end flat, call rates rise.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean 3-yr yields end flat, call rates rise.

text.p: Yields on three-year benchmark corporate bonds on Friday ended flat despite tight liquidity as dealers forecast fewer new issues for next week.

Three-month CD yields ended flat for the fourth consecutive day, but the overnight call rate average rose on tight liquidity as companies met Friday's deadline for value-added tax payments. * 3-yr corporates close unchanged at 12.52 pct * 3-mth CDs close unchanged at 13.10 pct * Overnight average call rate at 13.65 vs 12.96 pct
"Looking at the market factors yields should fall next week as money soaked up by the repos will be released," said Kang. "But some fear the central bank will siphon off the excess liquidity again."
Corporate bonds worth 28.5 billion won were issued on Friday dealer said.
